The Drive v2 resource ETag was observed to fence PATCH/PUT on three owned-file probes. That API capability does not establish full tunnel speed, durability across restarts, other accounts, or a permanent v2 contract.

Four Drive v2/control pipelined arms share one frozen binary; two Firestore/Drive hybrid pairs share a workload but the second uses a diagnostic-only source/binary revision. Their arm results are not pooled with clean-main HTTP-serial comparisons.

The Drive v2 phase trace is a single diagnostic arm: priority claims can contain multiple TLS frames; the trace identifies the four-unacknowledged per-stream admission bound for ten small text-stream physical fallbacks but does not prove per-frame latency causality.

The four-arm window 8/4/4/8 comparison shares one frozen binary and exact workload. Both window-8 arms improved text p95 and conservative units while upload file rate and warm-frame medians were worse; only two arms per setting and no saturated multi-stream fairness proof.

The FSH2 selective-receipt local prototype releases processed claims behind a stalled head, but adds 704 encoded bytes per snapshot and may cause extra metadata updates. Its fake-route two-arm mixed workload passed without establishing any Google speed or quota win.

The selected-project zero-limit contrast demonstrated independent Drive quota enforcement for one pinned-front metadata GET and one test grant, with final override removal and recovered read. It does not measure method unit weights, billing, sustained rate or 200,000-user capacity.

The v2 About and v3 start-page-token watermark primitive completed on one same-account pinned-front kit. In five of six mutations the exact list showed the change while a confirming signal read remained old. Both eventually advanced; neither is a sole correctness or low-latency discovery gate.
